skill.name: graphite-cli
skill.description: Guides Graphite CLI workflows for stacked pull requests, branch navigation, synchronization, and stack cleanup.
skill.summary: Use Graphite CLI commands to manage stacked pull requests and Git branch workflows.
skill.author: Calel33

security_audit.summary: All static findings are false positives caused by Markdown command examples in a Graphite CLI guide. No evidence of executable code, prompt injection, data exfiltration, or network reconnaissance was found.

remediation.issue: The guide describes commands that can push, rebase, amend, or delete branch state.
remediation.suggestion: Add explicit safety guidance to confirm the repository, branch, trunk, and remote before state-changing Graphite commands.

content.user_title: Manage Stacked Pull Requests with Graphite
content.value_statement: Stacked pull requests are hard to create, update, and synchronize consistently. This skill provides Graphite CLI workflows for branches, reviews, conflicts, and stack cleanup.
actual_capabilities: Explains Graphite CLI setup with gt auth and gt init.
Guides branch creation and PR submission with gt create and gt submit.
Describes stack navigation with log, up, down, top, bottom, and checkout commands.
Outlines synchronization, restacking, and conflict continuation workflows.
Covers stack changes such as move, fold, split, insert, and absorb.
References a detailed Graphite CLI guide for collaboration and multi-trunk use.
limitations: It provides workflow guidance and does not install Graphite CLI.
It cannot verify repository state without direct access to the local Git workspace.
It does not replace Graphite documentation for current product changes.
It should not run push, rebase, or branch deletion commands without user confirmation.

use_cases.title: Plan a Feature Stack
use_cases.description: Break a large feature into smaller dependent pull requests with clear branch order and review flow.

use_cases.title: Update Review Branches
use_cases.description: Apply feedback, amend commits, resubmit pull requests, and keep dependent branches aligned.

use_cases.title: Maintain a Clean Stack
use_cases.description: Synchronize with trunk, resolve conflicts, navigate branches, and clean up merged work.

prompt_templates.title: Learn the Basics
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain the basic Graphite CLI workflow for initializing a repository and creating my first stacked pull request.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Stack Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me split this feature into three Graphite pull requests and describe the branch order I should use.

prompt_templates.title: Handle Review Feedback
prompt_templates.prompt: I received review feedback on the middle branch of my stack. Guide me through updating it and resubmitting the stack.

prompt_templates.title: Repair a Complex Stack
prompt_templates.prompt: My Graphite stack is out of date with trunk and has conflicts. Give me a safe recovery sequence and explain each checkpoint.

output_examples.input: I need to ship a three-part feature with Graphite.
output: A branch sequence that starts from trunk and builds each pull request on the previous one.
A review plan that submits drafts first, then submits the full stack when the top branch is ready.
A cleanup step that synchronizes after merge and removes stale local branches when prompted.

output_examples.input: My stack has conflicts after syncing with trunk.
output: A checkpoint list for confirming the current branch and stack position before changes.
A conflict resolution flow that stages resolved files and continues the interrupted Graphite operation.
A verification step that reviews the stack shape before resubmitting pull requests.

output_examples.input: I need to change which branch another branch depends on.
output: A short explanation of when to move a branch versus inserting a new branch.
A safe sequence for checking the current stack, choosing the target parent, and validating the result.
A reminder to confirm before commands that rebase, fold, split, or push branches.

best_practices: Confirm the repository, trunk branch, and current branch before changing a stack.
Submit small, focused pull requests so each branch has a clear review purpose.
Synchronize regularly and verify the stack shape before pushing updates.
anti_patterns: Do not run Graphite commands in the wrong repository or on an unverified branch.
Do not fold, split, move, or absorb changes without understanding the stack impact.
Do not submit a full stack before checking branch order and review readiness.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps users plan and execute Graphite CLI workflows for stacked pull requests and branch management.

faq.question: Does it run Graphite commands automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance. Any command that changes repository state should require explicit user approval.

faq.question: Can it help with merge conflicts?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains the Graphite conflict flow for resolving files, staging changes, and continuing interrupted operations.

faq.question: Can it manage coworker stacks?
faq.answer: Yes. The included guide covers fetching, freezing, unfreezing, tracking, and building on shared stacks.

faq.question: What tools does it support?
faq.answer: The skill metadata lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: What should users verify first?
faq.answer: Users should verify the repository path, current branch, trunk branch, and remote target before push or rebase operations.
